name: vwap_reversion_5d
hypothesis: Stocks trading below their 5-day volume-weighted average price (VWAP) tend to revert upward over the next few days due to temporary selling pressure or liquidity imbalances, while stocks trading above their 5-day VWAP tend to revert downward.
economic_rationale: The VWAP over a medium horizon (5 days) serves as a proxy for the average transaction price of informed and uninformed traders. When the current price deviates significantly below this benchmark, it may indicate short-term overselling, prompting mean-reversion as liquidity providers step in. Conversely, prices far above VWAP may face profit-taking. This effect is expected to be stronger in liquid A-shares where temporary price impacts are corrected.
risk_notes: Crowding risk in mean-reversion strategies may reduce efficacy.
High sensitivity to market regime; momentum regimes can cause prolonged deviations.
Liquidity shocks or corporate actions may distort VWAP and close prices.
Transaction costs from frequent rebalancing can erode returns.
Factor may underperform in trending markets or during structural breaks.
iteration_note: Consider alternative windows (e.g., 10 or 20 days) or combining with volume or volatility filters to improve robustness.

name: vwap_reversion_10d
hypothesis: Stocks trading below their 10-day volume-weighted average price (VWAP) tend to revert upward over the next few days due to temporary selling pressure or liquidity imbalances, while stocks trading above their 10-day VWAP tend to revert downward.
economic_rationale: The VWAP over a longer horizon (10 days) serves as a more stable proxy for the average transaction price of informed and uninformed traders. When the current price deviates significantly below this benchmark, it may indicate short-term overselling, prompting mean-reversion as liquidity providers step in. Conversely, prices far above VWAP may face profit-taking. This effect is expected to be stronger in liquid A-shares where temporary price impacts are corrected, and the longer window may reduce turnover and noise.
risk_notes: Crowding risk in mean-reversion strategies may reduce efficacy.
High sensitivity to market regime; momentum regimes can cause prolonged deviations.
Liquidity shocks or corporate actions may distort VWAP and close prices.
Transaction costs from rebalancing can erode returns, though turnover may be lower than the 5-day version.
Factor may underperform in trending markets or during structural breaks.
Revision evaluated on the same sample remains in-sample and may overfit.
iteration_note: Revised the prior 5-day VWAP reversion factor to a 10-day window in response to high turnover diagnostics. This change aims to reduce turnover while maintaining the same economic idea. The revised factor has not been re-evaluated out-of-sample.
